symbols.name: K
symbols.def: cardinality of the terminal outcome alphabet

symbols.name: \mathcal Y
symbols.def: terminal outcome alphabet, ordered from worse to better

symbols.name: \mathcal T
symbols.def: the explicit depth-\(T\) SMART tree whose vertices retain their complete observed prefixes

symbols.name: h_\varnothing
symbols.def: the root node in the two-stage witness

symbols.name: \operatorname{ch}(h,a)
symbols.def: chance children reached after action \(a\) at node \(h\)

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.def: legal complete observed trajectories through \(\mathcal T\) ending in \(\mathcal Y\)

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: the full observed history at a decision node along \(O\)

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: binary intermediate response in the two-stage witness

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: candidate observed trajectory law used in confidence inversion

symbols.name: e_h(a)
symbols.def: SMART assignment kernel supplied on every legal node, including nodes having zero reach probability

symbols.name: \mathcal D
symbols.def: all deterministic maps selecting one element of \(\mathcal A(h)\) at every \(h\in\mathcal H\)

symbols.name: \Gamma_d
symbols.def: event that every realized treatment choice along \(O\) agrees with regime \(d\)

symbols.name: \mathcal C_h
symbols.def: all future potential histories and outcomes descending from node \(h\)

symbols.name: G(d)
symbols.def: the node-split graph induced by fixing regime \(d\) on \(\mathcal T\)

symbols.name: \sim_v
symbols.def: \((d,u)\sim_v(d',u')\) when the fixed inputs and random parent values for vertex \(v\) agree across \(G(d)\) and \(G(d')\)

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: a law on the complete finite counterfactual system indexed by \(\mathcal T\)

symbols.name: \kappa^d_{Q,v}
symbols.def: a version of the conditional law for vertex \(v\) in \(G(d)\); on a zero-probability parent fiber its value is arbitrary and is not constrained by the maintained FFRCISTG model

symbols.name: \bar\kappa_{Q,v}
symbols.def: a simultaneous all-fiber extension of the reached-history versions, selected by the dormant-kernel extension lemma

symbols.name: \mathfrak F(P)
symbols.def: observed-law-preserving complete FFRCISTG completions of \(P\) under ordinary reached-history single-world factorization and modularity

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: number of components in the local maximum problem

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: candidate local or root maximum law

symbols.name: g(h)
symbols.def: product of the probabilities \(e_{\tilde h}(\tilde a)\) along the treatment prefix of \(h\), with empty product one

symbols.name: F_h(k)
symbols.def: candidate CDF of the oracle continuation outcome at node \(h\)

symbols.name: G_{ha}(k)
symbols.def: candidate CDF after action \(a\) at node \(h\)

symbols.name: b_{ha}(k)
symbols.def: \(b_{ha}(k)=P(H=h,A_h=a,Y\leq k)/\{g(h)e_h(a)\}\) for a terminal action branch

symbols.name: \Theta(P)

symbols.name: L_P
symbols.def: lower oracle CDF envelope obtained by the backward recursion of Shahn2026Oracle

symbols.name: U_P
symbols.def: upper oracle CDF envelope obtained by the backward recursion of Shahn2026Oracle

symbols.name: V^-(P)
symbols.def: lower binary oracle value from Shahn2026Oracle

symbols.name: V^+(P)
symbols.def: upper binary oracle value from Shahn2026Oracle

symbols.def: trajectory laws satisfying \(p(H=h,A_h=a)=e_h(a)p(H=h)\) for every legal node-action pair

standard.name: Known sequential randomization in joint-kernel form
Sequential positivity with a finite-tree lower bound

assumptions.condition: \(Q(A_h=a,\mathcal C_h\in B,H=h)=e_h(a)Q(\mathcal C_h\in B,H=h)\quad\forall h\in\mathcal H,\ \forall a\in\mathcal A(h),\ \forall B\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\mathcal C_h)\)

standard.name: Strong sequential exchangeability in joint-kernel form
Observed-law compatibility of a counterfactual completion

definitions.name: Complete observed-law-preserving FFRCISTG completion class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(P)=\{Q:Q(O\in B)=P(O\in B)\ \forall B\subseteq\Omega,\ Q(O=O^d,\Gamma_d)=Q(\Gamma_d)\ \forall d\in\mathcal D,\ Q(A_h=a,\mathcal C_h\in B,H=h)=e_h(a)Q(\mathcal C_h\in B,H=h)\ \forall h,a,B,\ Q(O^d=x)=\prod_{v\in\mathcal V_d}\kappa^d_{Q,v}(x_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_d(v)})\ \forall d,x,\ \kappa^d_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid u)=\kappa^{d'}_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid u')\text{ whenever }(d,u)\sim_v(d',u')\text{ and both parent fibers have positive probability}\}\)

definitions.name: Local tree-diagonal capacity set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C(p_1,\ldots,p_m)=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal Y):F_q(k)\leq F_a(k)\ \forall a\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\ \forall k\in\mathcal Y,\ q(k)\leq\sum_{a=1}^m p_a(k)\ \forall k\in\mathcal Y\}\)

definitions.name: Intervention-reach rescaling
definitions.construction: \(g(h)=\prod_{(\tilde h,\tilde a)\prec h}e_{\tilde h}(\tilde a),\quad\rho_h=P(H=h)/g(h),\quad U_h(k)=\rho_hF_h(k),\quad V_{ha}(k)=\rho_hG_{ha}(k)\)

definitions.name: Tree-diagonal extended formulation
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R(P)=\{(q,\{U_h(k)\},\{V_{ha}(k)\}):U_h(-1)=V_{ha}(-1)=0,\ U_h(K-1)=V_{ha}(K-1)=\rho_h,\ \Delta U_h(k)\geq0,\ \Delta V_{ha}(k)\geq0,\ U_h(k)\leq V_{ha}(k),\ \Delta U_h(k)\leq\sum_{a\in\mathcal A(h)}\Delta V_{ha}(k),\ V_{ha}(k)=\sum_{h'\in\operatorname{ch}(h,a)}U_{h'}(k)\text{ on nonterminal branches},\ V_{ha}(k)=b_{ha}(k)\text{ on terminal branches},\ F_q(k)=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_0}U_h(k)\ \forall h,a,k\}\)

definitions.name: Pointwise oracle CDF envelope region
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm S}(P)=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal Y):L_P(k)\leq F_q(k)\leq U_P(k)\ \forall k\in\mathcal Y\}\), where \(L_P\) and \(U_P\) are the backward-recursion envelope CDFs of Shahn2026Oracle.

definitions.name: Whole-set confidence inversion
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal K_n=\{p\in\mathcal E_e:\lvert p(\omega)-\widehat p(\omega)\rvert\leq r_n\ \forall\omega\in\Omega\},\qquad\mathcal O_n=\{q:\exists p\in\mathcal K_n,\ \exists\{U_h(k)\},\{V_{ha}(k)\}\text{ such that }(q,\{U_h(k)\},\{V_{ha}(k)\})\in\mathcal R(p)\}\)

definitions.name: Positive two-stage nonrectangularity witness
definitions.construction: Take \(K=3\), one root \(h_\varnothing\), binary first and second actions, and \(Z\in\{0,1\}\). Set \(e_h(a)=1/2\), \(P^\star(A_{h_\varnothing}=a_0,Z=z)=1/4\), and the joint terminal cells \(P^\star(H=(a_0,z),A_{(a_0,z)}=a_1,Y=k)=r^\star(k)/8\) for every \(a_0,z,a_1\in\{0,1\}\), where \(r^\star=(0.45,0.05,0.50)\). Then \(L_{P^\star}(0)=L_{P^\star}(1)=0\), \(U_{P^\star}(0)=0.45\), and \(U_{P^\star}(1)=0.50\). For \(q^\star=(0.05,0.35,0.60)\), \(F_{q^\star}(0)=0.05\) and \(F_{q^\star}(1)=0.40\), so both coordinates are strictly interior. The child inequalities \(\Delta U_{(a_0,z)}(1)\leq\sum_{a_1=0}^1\Delta V_{(a_0,z),a_1}(1)\), propagated to the root, imply the excluding inequality \(q(1)\leq0.20\), whereas \(q^\star(1)=0.35\). The smallest envelope margin is \(0.05\), the capacity violation is \(0.15\), and every observed terminal cell is at least \(0.05/8\); continuity of the finite backward-envelope and capacity programs therefore gives a relative open neighborhood of \(P^\star\), inside the known-randomization affine model, on which these strict inequalities persist. For \(K>3\), redistribute a total mass \(\eta>0\) from outcome \(2\) among outcomes \(3,\ldots,K-1\) in every terminal kernel and in the candidate pmf, with \(\eta\) smaller than all three displayed strict margins; continuity preserves interiority and the exclusion while making every added outcome cell positive.

definitions.name: Response-function fiber-product lift handle
definitions.construction: Encode every finite one-step mechanism by categorical response functions; induct upward by coupling only incompatible action-subtree maxima and disintegrating each subtree on its assigned maximum. After the reached response system is assembled, invoke the dormant-kernel extension lemma on each \(\sim_v\)-equivalence class, assigning its unique reached value when one exists and an arbitrary common stochastic vector otherwise, then audit joint consistency and every single-world product formula on \(G(d)\).

statements.statement: For arbitrary \(p_1,\ldots,p_m\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\) and \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\), there exists a joint law of \((X_1,\ldots,X_m)\) with \(X_a\sim p_a\) and \(\max_a X_a\sim q\) if and only if \(q\in\mathcal C(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\). Every feasible \(q\) admits a finite monotone-residual transport and circle-cover sampler, and every infeasible \(q\) is separated by a violated displayed capacity inequality.
statements.justification: This is the exact cross-threshold compatibility result that turns scalar oracle bounds into one attainable law.
statements.gap: FanPark2010 Lemma 2.1 gives pointwise sharp bounds for the CDF of the static binary-treatment contrast \(Y(1)-Y(0)\) and explicitly notes that the resulting CDF envelopes need not be uniformly sharp; Artstein1983 gives general selection capacities and LaiRobbins1976 gives an extremal common-marginal construction. Ponomarev2024 Theorem 1 instead finds the smallest nonredundant Artstein collection for a supplied set-valued-prediction correspondence. None states this heterogeneous finite maximum-pmf iff: its closed-form lower-set and singleton-diagonal system characterizes one jointly attainable law across all thresholds and supplies an attaining sampler.
statements.consumer: Each decision node in the SMART recursion uses this criterion to propagate an entire continuation-outcome law rather than one threshold endpoint.

statements.statement: For every \(Q\in\mathfrak F(P)\) and every family of ordinary versions \(\{\kappa^d_{Q,v}\}\) satisfying single-world factorization and reached-history modularity, there exists a simultaneous completion \(\{\bar\kappa_{Q,v}\}\) on every legal parent configuration such that \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid d,u)=\kappa^d_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid u)\) on every positive-probability parent fiber, \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid d,u)=\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(\cdot\mid d',u')\) whenever \((d,u)\sim_v(d',u')\), and \(Q(O^d=x)=\prod_{v\in\mathcal V_d}\bar\kappa_{Q,v}(x_v\mid d,x_{\operatorname{pa}_d(v)})\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(x\in\Omega\). Thus all-fiber agreement is a selectable version completion, not an additional causal-model restriction.
statements.justification: The lemma separates harmless null-fiber version selection from the substantive global response-system lift.
statements.gap: RichardsonRobins2013SWIG constrains the FFRCISTG model on realized single-world distributions; the finite equivalence-class completion needed for an explicit dormant-coordinate construction is usually left implicit.
statements.consumer: The projection-and-lift theorem can use common dormant-fiber kernels without presenting that choice as a strengthened causal assumption.

statements.statement: For an observed law \(P\) satisfying known sequential randomization and \(e_h(a)\geq\varepsilon>0\) at every legal node-action pair, determine whether every \((q,\{U_h(k)\},\{V_{ha}(k)\})\in\mathcal R(P)\) has a single \(Q\in\mathfrak F(P)\) with \(q_Q=q\), including all dormant counterfactual branches and every joint consistency, randomization, reached-history modularity, and single-world product equality. The dormant-kernel extension lemma must then supply agreed \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}\) versions on zero-probability fibers without changing \(Q\). If universal lifting fails, determine the smallest finite tree and the additional separating facet required for exact projection.
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing local-to-global question; branchwise marginal preservation does not by itself construct a complete FFRCISTG response system, while null-fiber kernel agreement is handled separately by the extension lemma.
statements.gap: FanPark2010 stops at a static pair of potential outcomes, while Shahn2026Oracle Appendix A couples incompatible branches but leaves the complete dormant-coordinate construction implicit and GreseleEtAl2022 demonstrates that causal marginals can have nontrivial global compatibility restrictions. The first specifically dynamic step not covered by the static result is to couple action-specific continuation maxima at every full history and glue those conditional couplings across descendants into one complete FFRCISTG system.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution validates every sharpness and inference claim below; a negative resolution supplies the missing causal compatibility facet and prevents invalid SMART oracle bounds.

statements.statement: For every observed law \(P\in\Delta(\Omega)\) satisfying \(P(H=h,A_h=a)=e_h(a)P(H=h)\) and \(e_h(a)\geq\varepsilon>0\) for every legal node-action pair, let \(\mathfrak F(P)\) contain precisely the complete laws \(Q\) whose observed margin is \(P\) and on which joint consistency, joint sequential exchangeability, single-world factorization, and reached-history modularity hold. Then \(\Theta(P)=\operatorname{proj}_{q}\mathcal R(P)\). Moreover, every feasible array is attained by one \(Q\in\mathfrak F(P)\) whose complete counterfactual system contains every dormant branch; the dormant-kernel extension lemma selects agreed \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}\) versions on all zero-probability fibers without imposing an additional model restriction.
statements.justification: Projection equality makes the local capacity recursion a sharp causal identified set rather than a relaxation, while the separate extension lemma prevents null-fiber conventions from strengthening the model.
statements.gap: FanPark2010 sharply bounds a static two-potential-outcome contrast one threshold at a time, and Shahn2026Oracle proves dynamic endpoint constructions. Neither establishes equality between a whole recursively feasible pmf polytope and the projection of a complete FFRCISTG response system; the new step is the history-by-history coupling and global gluing of continuation maxima under ordinary reached-history modularity.
statements.consumer: SMART-BD investigators can interpret every feasible oracle-remission distribution as arising from a causally admissible response system with the observed trial law unchanged.

statements.statement: As a corollary of the projection-and-lift theorem, let \(N=\lvert\mathcal H\rvert\), \(A_\Sigma=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H}\lvert\mathcal A(h)\rvert\), and \(E=\sum_{h,a}\lvert\operatorname{ch}(h,a)\rvert\). The formulation \(\mathcal R(P)\) has \(O\{K(N+A_\Sigma)\}\) variables and constraints and \(O\{K(N+A_\Sigma+E)\}\) nonzero coefficients, all affine in observed multinomial probabilities. Membership of \(q\) and \(\sigma_P(c)\) have exact primal and strong-dual certificates, and any feasible solution yields a recursive attaining sampler.
statements.justification: The tree-sized fixed matrix makes full-law sharpness computationally usable once exact causal projection is established.
statements.gap: Russell2021 permits generic random-set and transport programs, GreseleEtAl2022 permits full response-function projection, and Ponomarev2024 minimizes the Artstein collection for a generic set-valued-prediction correspondence. None combines the maximum-specific local system with intervention reach and tree laminarity to obtain this dimension bound.
statements.consumer: A trial analyst can compute exact feasibility, quantile bounds, tail probabilities, or any linear oracle-law support value without enumerating exponentially many global response types.

statements.statement: For \(K\geq3\), there is a relatively open class of strictly positive two-stage binary-action SMART laws \(P\) for which \(\Theta(P)\subsetneq\mathcal B_{\mathrm S}(P)\). At the displayed witness, \(L_{P^\star}(0)=L_{P^\star}(1)=0\), \(U_{P^\star}(0)=0.45\), and \(U_{P^\star}(1)=0.50\), while \(F_{q^\star}(0)=0.05\) and \(F_{q^\star}(1)=0.40\). Thus \(q^\star\) is strictly inside the coordinatewise envelope, but the propagated tree-capacity facet \(q(1)\leq0.20\) excludes it because \(q^\star(1)=0.35\). The positive terminal-cell margin, envelope margin \(0.05\), and violation margin \(0.15\), together with continuity of the finite programs, preserve the separation on a relative open neighborhood of \(P^\star\) in the randomization model.
statements.justification: The explicit strict witness shows that the whole-law result contains identifying information invisible in every separate threshold interval.
statements.gap: Shahn2026Oracle establishes attainable envelope functions but does not display the interior geometry, the excluding cross-threshold tree facet, or a positive open set with strict nonrectangularity.
statements.consumer: Joint remission-threshold, quantile, and stochastic-dominance conclusions in SMART-BD can be certified without combining mutually incompatible pointwise bounds.

statements.statement: As a corollary of exact projection-and-lift and the compact fixed-matrix formulation, under independent sampling and known randomization, \(\Pr_P\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\mathcal O_n\}\geq1-\alpha\) for every \(n\geq1\) and every \(P\in\mathcal E_e\). Membership and every fixed linear support query for \(\mathcal O_n\) reduce to a linear program obtained by adjoining the constraints defining \(\mathcal K_n\) to \(\mathcal R(p)\).
statements.justification: The statement covers the entire random identified set in finite samples and remains valid at active-face ties.
statements.gap: HuangEtAl2017 handles static ordinal bound endpoints and OberReynolds2023 handles scalar transport values; neither gives finite-sample whole-polytope coverage for a longitudinal oracle distribution.
statements.consumer: SMART-BD can report an honest simultaneous region for every oracle-remission pmf, CDF, quantile, and prespecified linear summary.

statements.statement: When \(K=2\), projection of \(\mathcal R(P)\) onto \(q(1)\) equals the sharp interval \([V^-(P),V^+(P)]\) from Shahn2026Oracle, so the construction introduces no extra restriction in the binary-outcome special case.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against the known sharp binary recursion.
statements.gap: This is a compatibility corollary rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Existing binary oracle analyses can adopt the full-law machinery without changing their established endpoints.

sampling_model.design: Finite full-history sequential multiple-assignment randomized trial with the supplied kernel \(e_h(a)\), represented by the joint equalities \(P(H=h,A_h=a)=e_h(a)P(H=h)\).
sampling_model.treatment: At each reached node \(h\), treatment uses the known design kernel \(e_h\). The design supplies \(e_h\) at every legal node, including dormant nodes, while counterfactual conditional-kernel versions on null fibers are completed only by the theorem-level extension lemma.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance regression is required for finite-sample inversion; observed trajectory-cell probabilities enter the reach-rescaled linear program directly.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The CDF bounds are sharp for the complete distribution, with lower and upper envelope CDFs attained simultaneously across thresholds.
Distributions of selections of a random set are characterized by capacity inequalities.
For a common marginal, a maximally dependent coupling attains the extremal maximum survival function simultaneously at every threshold.
SWIG factorization gives the single-world Markov model corresponding to FFRCISTG and applies to dynamic treatment regimes.
Categorical response functions reduce the space of joint SCMs compatible with specified causal marginals.
Random-set and optimal-transport programs sharply bound continuous functionals of joint potential-outcome distributions.
Dual sample analogues of optimal-transport endpoints are root-\(n\) consistent and converge in distribution.
Inference for sharp ordinal treatment-benefit bounds must account for atom-driven nonregularity.

Lemma 2.1 gives pointwise best-possible lower and upper CDF bounds for the static binary-treatment effect \(Y(1)-Y(0)\) from its two marginal distributions, while the paper notes that these envelopes need not be uniformly sharp as an entire CDF.

Theorem 1 characterizes the smallest nonredundant collection of Artstein inequalities for a broad class of set-valued-prediction models, with a bipartite-connectivity algorithm for finite outcome spaces.
The graphical hierarchy distinguishes single-world intervention models from stronger cross-world intervention models.
The paper characterizes maximal bivariate copulas subject to a given continuous track section.

tldr: In a finite SMART, the observed law identifies each regime-outcome marginal but not the dependence needed for the perfect-information outcome \(M_Q=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}Y(d)\). The project characterizes every compatible discrete oracle-outcome pmf through local maximum-law capacity inequalities recursively linked over the full-history tree. Its field-tier headline is a projection-and-lift theorem universal over observed laws obeying known positive randomization: each recursively feasible array extends to one complete law \(Q\) preserving that observed margin, with consistency, exchangeability, single-world factorization, and reached-history modularity imposed on \(Q\). A separate kernel-extension lemma completes dormant zero-probability fibers without strengthening the causal model. Corollaries give a tree-sized polytope, exact certificates, attaining samplers, an explicit strictly nonrectangular positive witness, and finite-sample whole-set confidence inversion for oracle remission in SMART-BD.

project_justification.gap: Static sharp distributional bounds characterize pointwise limits for functions of two potential outcomes, and published oracle-DTR bounds identify sharp binary endpoints and two simultaneous CDF envelopes. Neither literature characterizes all attainable discrete oracle laws or verifies a complete dormant-branch lift for every interior law.
project_justification.niche: The ordered finite outcome support turns local coupling compatibility into a small capacity system, while the full-history SMART tree supplies a laminar recursion that generic response-type programs do not exploit.
project_justification.fill: For every observed law obeying known positive randomization, the tree-diagonal projection theorem equates this recursion with complete FFRCISTG laws whose observed margin is fixed and on which consistency, exchangeability, factorization, and reached-history modularity hold. A theorem-level finite kernel-extension argument coordinates null-fiber versions after the substantive lift, and the resulting corollaries compress the sharp set and map simultaneous multinomial uncertainty through the same program.

related_work: Shahn2026Oracle is the direct causal anchor: its Theorem 1 gives sharp binary oracle bounds, and Section 4 constructs two bounding CDFs for bounded outcomes. The present target is the distinct interior set of discrete oracle pmfs and its complete counterfactual lift. FanPark2010 Lemma 2.1 is the closest static sharp distributional-bounds comparator: it gives pointwise best-possible CDF bounds for \(Y(1)-Y(0)\) from two identified marginals and notes that the envelopes need not be uniformly sharp. Its static pairwise setting does not perform the first dynamic SMART-tree step here, namely coupling action-specific continuation maxima at every full history and gluing those conditional couplings across descendants into one observed-law-preserving complete FFRCISTG system. Artstein1983 provides the capacity-inequality language for random selections, and LaiRobbins1976 provides an extremal common-marginal maximum coupling; both inform the local construction without serving as claimed tightening targets. Ponomarev2024 Theorem 1 characterizes the smallest nonredundant Artstein-inequality collection for broad set-valued-prediction models and uses bipartite-graph connectivity in finite spaces. The local system here is structurally different: it targets the law of a maximum of heterogeneously margined coordinates, reduces locally to \(mK\) lower-set inequalities plus \(K\) singleton diagonal inequalities, and links them by mass conservation over a treatment tree; it does not claim to improve Ponomarev's minimal collection for his generic correspondence problem. RichardsonRobins2013SWIG fixes FFRCISTG semantics through single-world factorization and modularity on reached distributions; exact agreement of chosen conditional versions on dormant zero-probability fibers is supplied by a separate finite kernel-extension lemma. GreseleEtAl2022 supplies a finite response-function representation of categorical causal compatibility and motivates auditing global gluing. Russell2021 supplies the generic random-set and optimal-transport benchmark, whereas the treatment-tree formulation exploits reach rescaling and laminar structure. OberReynolds2023 and HuangEtAl2017 inform the inference layer. ShpitserTchetgen2016 clarifies why the result is stated under FFRCISTG and does not impose the stronger NPSEM-IE cross-world model.
technical_internal_limitation: The transport construction and reduced LP calculations are diagnostics, not established theorems. An independent finite response-type calculation matched the reduced formulation in 160 support directions over ten heterogeneous positive two-stage binary-action, binary-intermediate, three-outcome kernels, with maximum absolute discrepancy \(6.7\times10^{-16}\). This numerical kill test checks effective response-tree projection but does not certify the complete FFRCISTG response-system embedding. The separate dormant-kernel extension is finite equivalence-class bookkeeping once a reached response system exists; it does not resolve the global lift. Any recursively feasible point lacking such a lift invalidates the projection-and-lift statement and requires replacing \(\mathcal R(P)\) by the projected global polytope or adding the first missing facet. The claimed complexity is in explicit tree size; it is not polynomial in horizon under a compressed state representation.
honest_scope: The local finite maximum-law iff has a concrete monotone-residual transport route. The complete dormant-branch FFRCISTG response-system lift under known randomization, positivity, and ordinary reached-history modularity remains the genuine open content and is the premise for the compact-LP, sampler, nonrectangularity-as-an-identified-set, and inference corollaries. Exact agreement of kernel versions on dormant null fibers is a separate theorem-level extension problem and is not maintained as a causal assumption. The nonrectangularity witness displays its envelope coordinates, interior candidate, excluding facet, positive-cell margin, and relative open-neighborhood perturbation argument. Static continuous copula diagonals, unknown-randomization inference, restricted policy classes, missing outcomes, and NPSEM-IE tightening are outside the theorem claims. The binary reduction to Shahn2026Oracle is mandatory.

literature_map: The selected angle joins static distributional coupling, set-valued identification, and dynamic causal compatibility without treating any source as the proposed theorem. Shahn2026Oracle identifies recursive sharp endpoints for binary oracle success and constructs lower and upper CDF envelopes; Section 4 and Appendix A leave the interior discrete law set and a fully indexed dormant-branch response-system lift unstated. FanPark2010 Lemma 2.1 gives pointwise sharp static CDF bounds for a two-potential-outcome contrast and explains that those envelopes need not be uniformly sharp; it does not couple continuation maxima at each SMART history or glue the couplings through a dynamic tree. Artstein1983 supplies general capacity inequalities for random-set selections, while LaiRobbins1976 constructs an extremal maximum law for identical marginals; neither gives the heterogeneous finite pmf criterion used at every treatment node. Ponomarev2024 Theorem 1 finds the smallest nonredundant Artstein collection for broad set-valued-prediction correspondences, with a finite bipartite-connectivity algorithm. The proposed local inequalities instead characterize a maximum-law coupling with \(mK+K\) order and singleton constraints and are recursively tied by tree mass conservation; no improvement over Ponomarev's generic minimality theorem is claimed. RichardsonRobins2013SWIG supplies single-world factorization and reached-history modularity obligations on each completion \(Q\), not on the observed margin \(P\). A separate finite extension lemma selects common null-fiber versions after the reached system is built. GreseleEtAl2022 supplies the response-function projection benchmark and warns that separately admissible causal marginals need not glue globally. Russell2021 gives generic transport programs, but not a laminar tree-sized formulation. OberReynolds2023 concerns scalar transport endpoints rather than finite-sample containment of an entire dynamic oracle-law set. OmladicSkulj2026 occupies bivariate continuous track sections, so no static copula novelty is claimed.

novelty_justification: The closest static sharp distributional result is FanPark2010: Lemma 2.1 gives pointwise best-possible CDF bounds for a function of two potential outcomes but does not characterize one entire attainable law and has no dynamic tree. The first new dynamic step is to couple action-specific continuation maxima conditional on each full history and then glue all such couplings across descendants into one complete observed-law-preserving FFRCISTG system. The closest causal result is Shahn2026Oracle: it proves scalar recursive bounds and exhibits two simultaneous envelope distributions, whereas the present kernel asks for the entire attainable discrete pmf set, including the displayed cross-threshold restriction that excludes a CDF strictly between those envelopes. Ponomarev2024 characterizes the smallest nonredundant Artstein collection for broad set-valued-prediction correspondences; the proposed local system is not a rival generic selection theorem, but a structurally different \(mK+K\)-inequality maximum-law characterization linked by conservation constraints over a SMART tree. Russell2021 supplies a generic random-set and transport benchmark, whereas the present kernel seeks an exact formulation linear in \(K\) times explicit treatment-tree size. The decisive novelty is the projection equality between that local tree-diagonal capacity system and complete FFRCISTG laws \(Q\), universally over observed laws \(P\) satisfying known positive randomization, with consistency, exchangeability, factorization, and reached-history modularity imposed on each \(Q\). The dormant-null-fiber version completion is isolated as a theorem-level lemma rather than encoded as an assumption. The compact formulation and inference results are explicit corollaries of the projection-and-lift theorem.
